rules: A scheduled slot that cannot reach verified publication is not discarded; it becomes publication debt.
Publication debt survives date changes and PC power-off periods until buyer-visible publication is verified.
The next available production/publication run must service accumulated debt before treating the current day's quota as satisfied.
One run may complete multiple publications when debt exists; five per catch-up cycle is a pacing preference, not a lifetime or daily production cap.
Do not count queue insertion, local publisher success logs, editor/admin URLs, drafts, or unverified pages as completed publications.
Cloud-side planning and queue production should continue while the Windows PC is off; local publishing catches up when the PC is next available.
If the PC is powered off for an entire calendar day, publication on that exact calendar day cannot be guaranteed; the missed quota must be caught up automatically on the next available PC session.
Do not silently lower daily targets because of outages or missed schedules.
Do not disable BOOTH cloud automation because of a recoverable publication or verification delay.
